audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with the packet, and rows 5 and 6 also contradicted this page's own prose: win[5] said Pantheon while whys[5], spikes[2] and content.late all say the lane flips to Yasuo at first item.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Yasuo, Pantheon, Yasuo, Yasuo] and the mirror (pantheon__yasuo) already moved its row 6 to Yasuo. Row 0 said Skill while whys[0] says 'Level 1 is Pantheon's'. Every flip here brings a row into line with both the packet and the text already on the page.
audit.corrected: Proposed rows 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 as paired flips (phases[N].side + win[N]) in one atomic group with matching ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] described level 5 in the row labelled Level 6, and no spike carried a cooldown number.
audit.why: Row 4 is Level 6, where Grand Starfall (180s at rank 1) and the W all-in are the actual spike. Comet Spear is 11s at rank 1, Shield Vault 13s, Aegis Assault 22s — those are the numbers that make 'trade on his cooldown' actionable.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[4] as the Level 6 read, whys[3] as the 4-5 row, and wrote the three real cooldowns into spikes[1].text, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d and dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aegis Assault appeared nowhere on the page, and the page implied Last Breath needs someone else to launch you.
audit.why: Two decisive interactions were missing. First, Aegis Assault is a channel that makes him invulnerable to damage from the front — any CC cancels it, and Yasuo's two-stack Steel Tempest knockup is exactly that, so his 22s defensive cooldown is yours to delete. Second, that same third Steel Tempest is a knockup in Yasuo's own kit, so Last Breath is a live 1v1 threat at 6 with no ally required — the mirror flagged the opposite reassurance as its most important correction.
audit.corrected: Wrote the Aegis Assault cancel into spikes[1].text, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns, and the self-setup knockup into spikes[1].text and spikes[3].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named only Comet Spear, and report[5] implied the wall answers his engage.
audit.why: Shield Vault is a 600-range point-and-click dash stun with an auto reset — no projectile, so Wind Wall never stops it. Spending the wall on the engage instead of the spear is the losing line, and the page half-suggested it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d and content.late now split the blockable spear from the unblockable stun.

edits.before: Grand Starfall (R) gives him roam and all-in pressure, but you steal tempo — level 4 already swings your way with your dash spacing, and by 6 you can bait his W stun, block the Q with Wind Wall, and punish. Hold Wind Wall for his engage, not his poke.

edits.before: You out-scale him cleanly — Pantheon's damage plateaus while yours explodes with crit. His only threat is a Grand Starfall flank or a W stun to start a fight, so save Wind Wall for the engage and don't get caught by his point-and-click stun.
edits.after: You out-scale him cleanly — Pantheon's damage plateaus while yours explodes with crit. Your third Steel Tempest sets up your own Last Breath, so you never need a team knockup — just do not get caught by his Shield Vault stun.

edits.before: From first item on the matchup is yours: crit Yasuo out-scales a Pantheon whose damage plateaus, so block his Q, dodge the W stun, and out-duel him. Late-game his only threat is a flank engage — hold Wind Wall for it.
edits.after: From first item on the matchup is yours: crit Yasuo out-scales a Pantheon whose damage plateaus. Wind Wall's 25s eats Comet Spear but never the Shield Vault dash, so spend it on the spear and sidestep the stun.

notes: Aegis Assault was completely absent from this page despite being the cooldown that decides every all-in: it is a channel, so the two-stack Steel Tempest knockup cancels it, and it only blocks damage from the front. Grand Starfall carries a projectile flag but Riot's text describes a leap that lands as a comet, so I made no claim that Wind Wall stops it. Five chart rows realigned to the packet and mirror as one atomic paired group; rows 5 and 6 were also contradicting this page's own first-item prose before the flip.
